judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade R (rank 0, resolved coordinates). The first is Term 2, Emergent Reading / Shared Reading: 'Draws pictures capturing the main idea of stories, songs or rhymes' (LC tags: drawing, main idea, rhymes, stories). The second is Term 4, Listening and Speaking (Oral) / Daily activities: 'Listens to longer stories and shows understanding by answering questions related to the story', decomposed into 'Listens to longer stories' and 'Shows understanding by answering questions related to the story'. They cohere substantively as two complementary Grade R ways of demonstrating comprehension of narrative text — a non-verbal, representational gist response during shared reading and an oral, question-answering response during listening — so this is more than generic repetition or shared hierarchy/LC overlap. But the evidence does not establish a developmental dependency: the endpoints sit in different Skill Areas and Sub-strands, use different input channels and response modes, and the increased demand in the Term 4 statement (longer texts, explicit verbal questioning) belongs to the oral listening strand rather than extending the drawing-of-main-idea capability. The nomination signals are weak (one shared LC tag 'stories', token/trigram jaccard ~0.08-0.10, weak rank proximity with rank_gap 0), which supports coherence but not a buildsTowards claim in either direction; relatesTo is symmetric and retains canonical endpoint order with null direction. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 (rank 3) Skills in the Reading and Phonics skill area, but in different sub-strands and terms: the first is Term 4 Shared Reading ('Reads written texts as a whole class with the teacher (shared reading) and discusses characters, the ‘problem’ in the story, the plot and the values in the text'), the second is Term 2 Paired/Independent Reading ('Reads independently books read in Shared Reading sessions, simple story books and books from the reading corner ... at the independent reading level of the children'). They are substantively coherent and mutually reinforcing: the Term 2 independent-reading statement explicitly re-reads texts first met in Shared Reading, so the two sub-strands are complementary practices on the same texts. The pedagogically natural dependency runs from teacher-led shared reading to independent re-reading, i.e. from the later Term 4 node to the earlier Term 2 node, which is not an admissible within-grade direction; and the reverse (independent reading practice in Term 2 enabling whole-class discussion of character, plot and values in Term 4) is not specifically supported by the evidence, since the Term 4 statement adds literary discussion rather than extending independent reading capability. Symmetric relatesTo therefore fits the evidence better than either buildsTowards direction. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, but the full statement text and identity scopes are present, so the judgment is not materially impaired.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are the identical CAPS bullet 'Reads aloud to a partner' under Reading and Phonics > Paired/Independent Reading: the first at Grade 3 (rank 3) Term 3, the second at Grade 2 (rank 2) Term 2. The supplied source refs show the same bullet text and near-identical row context describing the daily 20-minute paired/independent reading routine alongside guided reading; the only differentiating evidence is the grade and term banner. There is no pair-specific indication of expanded capability (no longer or more complex texts, no added independence, no broadened text range) attached to the Grade 3 statement, and the 'graded reading series' reference actually occurs in the Grade 2 row context rather than the Grade 3 one, so buildsTowards would rest on repeated wording plus grade rank alone, which is not sufficient in this deliberately repetitive curriculum. The recurrence is nevertheless substantive rather than generic: it is the same paired oral-reading practice deliberately re-stated in the same sub-strand of the same skill area at an adjacent grade, giving genuine instructional coherence and reinforcement between the two statements. Canonical relatesTo with null direction is therefore the complete judgment; endpoint order is technical and non-semantic. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Emergent Reading skills under a Phonological/Phonemic Awareness sub-strand, using clapping as the segmentation technique, but they sit in different terms and at different grain sizes. The second SFI (Grade R, Term 1) has learners clap each word in an oral sentence where all words have only one syllable, i.e. word-level segmentation with the syllable deliberately held constant. The first SFI (Grade R, Term 2) extends this to clapping or drum beats on each syllable within multisyllabic words ('ba-na-na', 'Lu-ne-tta' has three claps, 'Rose' one clap), requiring segmentation of units inside a single word and counting of those units. This is pair-specific deepening (word unit to sub-word syllable unit, plus counting), not mere repeated wording, and the Term 1 clapping/word-boundary competence plausibly supports success with Term 2 syllable division. Direction is earlier Term 1 to later Term 2 within Grade R, consistent with the configured term order. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, but the full statement texts and identity scopes (grade/term/skill area/sub-strand) are present and unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 Skills (rank 3). The first, 'Writes three short sentences dictated by teacher', sits in Term 1 under Reading and Phonics > Phonics, exercising accurate sentence-level transcription (spelling, sentence boundaries, punctuation) with full teacher scaffolding. The second, 'Writes and illustrates sentences on a topic to contribute to a book for the class library', sits in Term 3 under Writing > Shared, Group and Independent Writing and requires the learner to generate and present their own sentences on a chosen topic for an audience. The change is pair-specific and substantive: from teacher-dictated content to self-generated, topic-focused, audience-directed writing with illustration, while retaining the shared sentence-writing core (LC tags/text overlap on 'sentences', 'writing', 'writes'). Secure sentence-writing accuracy in Term 1 plausibly supports success with independent sentence composition in Term 3; the direction Term 1 -> Term 3 within the same Grade is permitted. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so only the bounded excerpts and ancestry were judged.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0), Skill Area Emergent Writing, Sub-strand Emergent Handwriting, so direction must come from Term order within the grade. The second SFI is anchored to Term 3 ('Develops eye-hand co-ordination: plays catch ..., creates drawings, makes more complex patterns with crayons'), and the first SFI is anchored to Term 4 ('Traces simple outlines of pictures, patterns and own names where the correct starting point and writing direction are indicated on letters'). This is not mere repeated wording: the Term 3 statement builds gross/fine eye-hand co-ordination and free pattern-making with crayons, while the Term 4 statement requires more controlled pencil work constrained by a given outline, a specified starting point and writing direction, including the learner's own name. Proficiency in the earlier co-ordination and pattern-making work plausibly supports success in the later directional tracing, giving an earlier-Term to later-Term buildsTowards within Grade R. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence, and the Term 4 endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, so the judgment rests on the quoted statement text and resolved Grade/Term/Sub-strand scopes supplied.

judgment.rationale: The second SFI (Grade R, rank 0, Term 2, Emergent Writing / 'Works with words': 'Groups words that share the same initial sound or letter') is emergent phonological/alphabetic awareness in which learners attend to an initial sound and its corresponding letter in whole words. The first SFI (Grade 1, rank 1, Term 3, Reading and Phonics / Daily Phonic Activities: 'Identifies letter-sound relationships of all single letters') is a substantively expanded, systematic requirement covering the full set of single letters rather than only the initial position of grouped words, and it is taught as explicit daily phonics rather than incidental sorting. Facility with hearing and matching initial sounds to letters plausibly supports success in identifying letter-sound correspondences for all single letters, so the permitted lower-to-higher direction (Grade R to Grade 1) is justified; this is more than shared 'letter'/'sound' wording or the weak rank-proximity and LC tag overlap that nominated the pair. Evidence limits: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so only the bulleted statement text and identity scope were assessable, and both endpoints and all ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (grade and term banners merged from repeated printed headers).

They sit in the same grade and Skill Area but under different sub-strands and address different capabilities: oral reading fluency/prosody versus an independent word-meaning reference strategy. Neither statement's text, LCs (fluency/expression/guided reading vs dictionary/meanings/vocabulary) nor source rows show that proficiency in one is a developmental support for the other, so no buildsTowards direction is justified despite the Term 2 to Term 4 ordering; the nomination signals are only a shared Grade ancestor, a single shared LC tag 'reading' and the token 'and'. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the first endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, so unseen source detail could alter this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0) but in different skill areas and terms: the first is Term 4 Listening and Speaking (Oral) under 'Daily activities...' and requires listening to and recalling simple word sequences ('spark', 'bark', 'cart', 'start'), building from three to four or more words — an auditory sequential memory / phonological attention task; the second is Term 2 Emergent Reading under 'Emergent reading', requiring listening to and discussing stories and other texts read aloud, recalling details and stating the main idea — narrative comprehension (LCs: listens to, discusses, recalls details, states main idea). A buildsTowards from the first (Term 4) to the second (Term 2) is invalid within one grade; the reverse direction (Term 2 story comprehension towards Term 4 word-sequence recall) is not substantively supported, since text comprehension is not evidence of supporting short-term auditory memory for phonologically similar words — the shared signal is only the generic 'listens'/'recalls' wording and LC tags 'listening'/'recall'. The pair does, however, show coherent, mutually reinforcing attentive-listening and recall development across oral language and emergent reading in the same grade, so a symmetric relatesTo is the best-supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the bounded excerpts shown.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 1, Term 4, WRITING, sub-strand 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' bullets from the same printed table row (page index 81), so coordinate rank is identical (Grade 1) and no term ordering distinguishes them. 'Begins to use present and past tense correctly in writing' is an emergent grammatical-accuracy skill in composing text; 'Contributes ideas for and helps to revise a class/group story (Shared Writing)' is a collaborative composition/revision skill whose LCs cover idea contribution and revising. They cohere substantively — revising a shared class story is a natural context for attending to verb tense, and tense control supports clearer contributions — but the evidence shows neither as a dependency or developmental precondition for the other, and same-rank, same-term placement provides no substantive directional warrant. Shared ancestry and the single shared token 'writing' alone would not establish a relation; the complementary composition/accuracy coherence does. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so only the bounded excerpts were used.

judgment.rationale: The Grade R Term 2 item sits under EMERGENT WRITING / 'Emergent Writing:' and is 'Draws pictures to convey a message such as own \u2018news\u2019' (LC tags: drawing, emergent writing, message, news); the Grade 1 Term 4 item sits under LISTENING AND SPEAKING (ORAL) and is 'Talks about personal experiences and feelings such as tells news' (LC tags: feelings, news, personal experiences, speaking). They cohere substantively around the CAPS 'news' practice of communicating one's own personal experience, but in different modalities and different skill areas: pictorial message-making versus oral recounting of experiences and feelings. The evidence shows no pair-specific developmental dependency \u2014 competence in drawing a news picture is not what enables oral news-telling (oral news-telling is itself an established Foundation Phase oral routine), and the nomination rests mainly on the shared token 'news' plus weak Grade R\u2192Grade 1 rank proximity, which alone cannot establish buildsTowards. Symmetric conceptual/representational coherence around the same communicative content is best captured as relatesTo. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded excerpts shown.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 Skills (rank 1) but in different Skill Areas and Terms: the first is Term 2 Listening and Speaking ('Joins in the choruses of songs, stories, rhymes', LC tags choruses/participation/rhymes/songs) and the second is Term 1 Reading and Phonics ('Begins to use blending to make words... identifying the rhymes', LC tags blending/phonics/rhymes/word building). They share genuine phonological-awareness coherence around rhyme: oral chorusing of songs and rhymes gives the aural rhyme exposure that complements explicit rhyme identification during blending work. However, the only developmental direction that could be argued (oral rhyme participation supporting phonic rhyme identification) runs from the Term 2 statement back to the Term 1 statement within the same grade, which is not a valid buildsTowards direction; and the admissible forward direction (blending/word building supporting joining in choruses of songs) is not pedagogically supported by the evidence, since choral participation does not depend on decoding. Complementary, mutually reinforcing rhyme work without a justified dependency therefore warrants relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all involved SFIs carry upstream audit/merge context, so this judgment rests on the bounded excerpts supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 2 (rank 2) Reading and Phonics / 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes:' Skills, but source refs place the first in Term 1 ('Revises word families with short vowel sounds: -at, -ag, -am, -it') and the second in Term 3 ('Groups common words into sound families such as "oy", "oi"; "ay", "ai"'). The forward Term 1 -> Term 3 direction within the same grade is permitted. This is not mere repetition: the Term 1 statement revises simple short-vowel rime families (single-letter vowels), while the Term 3 statement extends the same word-grouping-by-sound strategy to vowel digraphs/diphthongs with alternative spellings of one sound, a substantively more complex orthographic pattern. Facility in sorting words into short-vowel families supports success in grouping words into digraph sound families, so first_to_second buildsTowards is supported. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so term placement rests on the supplied identity_scope values.
